scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! The IT department is OFF THE NETWORK --
every single one of our 192.168.1.x machines, all at once, can't reach
anything!! It's the switch box all our wires go into (switch0) -- it is DEAD,
one hundred percent. All of us going down at the same moment means the one
box we share died, there is no other explanation!! Please restart switch0,
and if it doesn't wake up REPLACE it -- the whole department is sitting here
doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Switching and routing for the IT department (192.168.1.0/24) are operating normally. Direct evidence: multiple IT hosts have link and valid IP/gateway (e.g., it_hod 192.168.1.2/24, it_lab1 192.168.1.3/24) with default via 192.168.1.1, and can ping their gateway router0 (0% loss, sub‑ms RTT). Cross‑subnet reachability also works from IT to Office (192.168.3.2), Principal (192.168.4.2), Servers (1.0.0.5), and Internet LAN (128.168.0.2/.0.3) with 0% loss. The alleged dead switch0 is up and forwarding: its bridge br0 and member ports eth0 (uplink to router0) and eth1 (to lan_it) are UP/RUNNING, with RX/TX counters incrementing.

Mechanism: If switch0 or the IT gateway were down, IT hosts could not reach 192.168.1.1 or each other; our probes show the opposite. Router0’s interface eth0 is up at 192.168.1.1/24 with RIP routes to other LANs, explaining successful inter‑LAN pings.

Localization: No fault found on switch0 (br0, eth0, eth1), router0 (eth0), or on sampled IT hosts’ NICs. Connectivity throughout the IT segment and to other subnets is healthy.

Root cause: The report appears to be a false positive or a transient/user‑side/application issue, not a switching failure.

Corrective fix: No restart or replacement of switch0 is warranted. Advise checking client OS/network status (DNS, firewall, application servers) and capturing traceroute/ping at incident time. If symptoms recur, collect switch0 port counters/MAC table and router0 ICMP/DNS reachability to correlate.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly reports 0% loss pings to gateway 192.168.1.1 and states IT hosts can reach each other and other subnets, confirming the 192.168.1.0/24 baseline is healthy.

The inference chain (reachable hosts ⇒ switch forwarding OK ⇒ report likely false positive) is logical and the key checks were performed.
